blocks.text: What an AI assistant for Linear on Mac does

Lazur is a voice assistant that sits in the notch at the top of your Mac. You hold ⌥⌘, ask a question, and it reads what is on your screen. It answers out loud. It can also point at a control, walk you through a task step by step, draft text, and dictate text at your cursor. Those are the five jobs this page covers.

Lazur works from the screen at the moment you ask. If an issue is closed or scrolled out of view, Lazur cannot see it. Open the issue first, then hold the keys. This is the first thing to check when an answer feels off.

items: Explain: ask what a status, label, or panel means. Lazur answers from what it can read.
Point: ask where a control is. Lazur circles it and draws a label beside it.
Guide: ask for steps. Lazur gives one step, then waits for your click before the next one.
Draft: ask for text. Lazur writes it and types it at the cursor.
Dictate: hold fn and speak. Clean, formatted text appears at the cursor.

blocks.text: Lazur does not click buttons, edit issues, or operate Linear for you. It is not a plugin or add-in. Lazur is not built by Linear and has no partnership with it. You make every change yourself, and Lazur helps you find the right place to make it.
Where people get stuck in Linear on Mac

Linear's docs list many keyboard shortcuts, but the shortcuts are spread across several pages. Users still get stuck. G2 has 127 reviews of Linear, and the same cons repeat. The most common are limited features (6 mentions), missing automation and epic management (5), limited customization (5), and lack of intuitiveness (4).

Those counts are small. Six mentions out of 127 reviews is a pattern, not a survey. Reviewers choose what to write, so the list leans toward people who were annoyed enough to post. Use it as a pointer for where to look, not as proof of how common a problem is.
Lack of intuitiveness is where a voice assistant can help. When a control is hard to find, you can ask where it is. You do not need to read a help page first.
Ask what is on screen: explain statuses and views

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a plain question. Lazur reads the screen and answers out loud. Say you have an issue open with the status In Review and a High priority label. Ask, what does In Review mean here? Lazur answers from what it can see, such as the status name and the other fields on the issue. It cannot see your team's workflow settings unless those settings appear on screen.

Explain mode is strongest on busy screens. A triage view, a filtered board, or an issue with many labels is hard to scan. Ask which of the visible issues are blocked. Lazur answers from what is on screen. If the list runs past the bottom of the window, it may miss items that are scrolled away.

Avoid asking about content you have not opened. Lazur answers from the screen as it is now. If you need the full description, open the issue and let it load first. A half-loaded page produces a half-right answer.
Ask where a control is: point and circle

Ask, where is the board toggle? Lazur circles the control on your screen and draws a label beside it. In Linear, the board toggle switches between board and list layout. Linear's board layout docs list ⌘B for it. You press the key yourself, so you learn the shortcut while you see where the control sits.

Pointing helps most with controls that have no clear label. Linear's select issues docs say ⌘K opens the command bar. If the bar is closed, Lazur has nothing to circle. Press ⌘K first, then ask what you can do from it.

Lazur circles the button. You click it. That split matters. You stay in control of the issue, and you learn where things live. Use the circles to learn the layout, then move to the shortcut list below.
Walk through a feature one step at a time

Guide mode fits tasks with several steps. Ask, walk me through moving an issue to the top of its column. Lazur gives you one step, then waits until you finish it. It does not move ahead on its own. The steps below follow Linear's board layout docs, so you can check them against the page.

items: Press ⌘B until you see the board layout.
Press X to select the issue you want to move.
Press ⌥⇧↑ to move the selected issue to the top of its column.

blocks.text: Two notes. Linear's docs describe the move for one selected issue, so test it before you move a group. Shift+X adds issues to a selection, so check that the selection looks right before you press the move key.
When you press the wrong key, say so. Ask, I pressed the wrong key, what now? Lazur looks at the screen again and picks up from there. That works better than starting the whole walkthrough over.
Dictate text at the cursor in Linear

Hold fn and speak. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text and types it where the cursor sits. That works in an issue title, a comment box, or a description field. Dictation is included with Lazur. Pro and Power both list it as unlimited.

Set up the personal dictionary once. Add product names, team names, and people's names that dictation tends to mishear. Snippets handle text you type often, such as a bug template. Clipboard slots hold text you copy from another tab, so you can paste it into an issue without switching back.
Click into the field first. The cursor needs to sit where you want the text. A common mistake is holding fn with the cursor in the search bar, then wondering where the text went.
Speak in short sentences. Long run-on speech makes the cleanup harder. Read the result before you submit, especially for numbers, version strings, and issue IDs.
Draft a bug report from what you just described

Lazur drafts text and types it at the cursor. Use it when you know what broke but do not want to write the report from scratch. Say, draft a bug report from what I just described, with steps to reproduce and the expected and actual result. Lazur writes it from your words and what is on screen, then types it into the field.

Linear added an Insert screenshot option to the macOS desktop slash menu, according to a September 24, 2026 changelog entry. Lazur does not insert the image for you. You open the slash menu, choose the option, and pick the file. If you lose the option, ask Lazur to circle it.
Drafts reflect what you told Lazur. They do not check the facts. Compare the steps with what happened on your machine. A draft can sound right and still list the wrong version or the wrong view.
Linear keyboard shortcuts to learn first

Shortcuts are the fastest route through Linear. The table below uses Linear's own docs wherever it can. Linear does not publish a full shortcut list, and third-party lists disagree on the total. Treat any list that claims to be complete with some doubt.

rows: Switch between board and list layout
Board layout and select issues docs
Move a selected issue to the top or bottom of its column
blocks.caption: Shortcuts from Linear's docs, except C, which comes from a third-party site.

blocks.text: Arrow keys and J and K move the highlight in select mode. Press X when the highlight sits on the issue you want. Esc clears the selection, so you do not need to click away.

Avoid assuming board and list shortcuts match. Linear says they are almost exactly the same, with a few exceptions. The docs do not name the exceptions. Test a shortcut in the view you use most before you rely on it.
Recent Linear changes that affect shortcuts

Linear's changelog moves quickly. Several recent entries touch how you move around. On September 3, 2026, Cmd or Ctrl+N started choosing what to create from the current view. A desktop fix from the same entry stopped opening a document from navigating to its parent. On November 5, 2026, Cmd or Ctrl+click on an open page switches to its desktop tab, and Shift+click opens a new tab.

The September 3 entry lists several items without a date for each one. Treat that date as approximate. If a shortcut seems off after an update, ask Lazur to point at the control instead of trusting an old list.
Linear plan limits and per-user costs

Linear's Free plan costs $0. It has unlimited members, but only 2 teams, 250 issues, and 10MB file uploads. Basic costs $10 per user per month when billed yearly. It includes 5 teams and unlimited issues. Business costs $16 per user per month when billed yearly, with unlimited teams, private teams and guests, and 15 release pipelines.

Quick math helps. Take your seat count and multiply it by $10 for Basic or $16 for Business, billed yearly. Those are list prices from Linear's pricing page, so check the page before you buy. Plan limits can change.

Lazur has its own plans, and they include AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both. Current prices and limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing). Pick a plan after you see what you use in a normal week, not before.
Avoid buying Business because it sounds safer. If your team fits within Basic limits, the extra cost pays for features you may not use yet.
What Lazur sees and sends from your Mac

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.

Linear issues can hold customer names, unreleased plans, and security details. Hold the shortcut only when you need help. Close or hide anything sensitive before you ask about the whole screen. A notification or a chat window in the corner counts as on screen too.

Permissions matter. macOS asks for microphone and screen access. Lazur cannot hear you or see the screen without them. If an answer comes back blank, check those permissions before you blame the question.
Which Macs and macOS versions work with Lazur and Linear

Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Linear's Mac desktop app supports both chip types too. Linear announced its Apple silicon build on March 18, 2021. It said the M1 binary runs without emulation, which makes the app run faster.

Linear's download page says the desktop app shows notifications through the operating system and stays in the Dock with unread alerts. It also says there is less risk of conflicting with browser shortcuts. The page does not list a version number or a minimum macOS version. Third-party sites disagree on the minimum, so check Linear's download page and About This Mac before you update.
Windows is not available for Lazur. It is planned, not shipped. If your team uses Linear on Windows, Lazur cannot help there yet.
Mistakes that waste the first week

items: Asking about an issue that is closed or scrolled away. Open it and let it load first.
Expecting Lazur to change an issue. It explains and points. You make the change.
Skipping the permission prompts. Lazur cannot hear or see without them.
Dictating into the wrong field. Click into the field before you hold fn.
Treating G2 complaint counts as a survey. They are small and self-selected.
Trusting an old shortcut list. Linear's changelog changed shortcut behavior in 2026.

blocks.text: What to do next

Start small. Open an issue in the Linear desktop app, hold ⌥⌘, and ask what one field means. Then ask where the board toggle is. Then dictate one sentence into a comment. Those three steps cover the basic jobs.

If your work follows a specific role, the role pages show how teams use Linear day to day. Product managers can read the [Linear for product managers on Mac page](/for/product-managers/linear). QA testers can start with the [software QA testers page](/for/software-qa-testers/linear). When you are ready, get Lazur from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Is Lazur made by Linear?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a separate Mac voice assistant. Linear did not build it, and Lazur has no partnership with Linear. It is not a plugin or add-in for Linear. It works from the screen the same way it works in other apps.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the Linear desktop app or only in a browser?
faq.answer: Lazur works from the screen, so it can read whatever Linear shows you. Linear's desktop app runs on Intel and Apple Silicon Macs, and Lazur runs on both chip types too.

faq.question: Can Lazur create or edit issues for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It explains, points, guides, and drafts or types text when you ask. You make the change in Linear.

faq.question: Which keys start Lazur?
faq.answer: Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor.

faq.question: Do I need a Linear plan to use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur is a separate product from Linear. Linear's Free plan has limits of 2 teams and 250 issues, and Lazur does not change those limits. Check the Linear pricing page for Linear plans and the Lazur pricing page for Lazur plans.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my Linear content to AI providers?
faq.answer: When you ask a question, Lazur sends the audio and the screenshot to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Why did Lazur circle the wrong control?
faq.answer: Pointing depends on what is visible. Scroll, open the right panel, or switch to the right view, then ask again. Linear's board and list layouts place some controls in different spots.
